positions.name: FerryLateSailingWeekdayVsWeekend
positions.frame: how should the last ferry's departure time be set on weekdays versus weekends, given how many passengers each late sailing actually carries?
positions.why: Both statements read the same timetable question through observed late-sailing ridership. The weekday statement moves the last sailing earlier because it carries under ten passengers a night. The weekend statement leaves the timetable alone because Friday and Saturday sailings still fill. The two pull in different directions (cut versus keep) but rest on the same demand evidence, so the frame holds both sides without resolving them.

placements.why: No existing leaf covers ferry service times. The tool library leaf is the nearest, since hours there also follow where users turn up, but it is about a different service and carries a staffing clause. The weekday cut (under ten passengers a night) and the weekend hold (Friday and Saturday still fill) both rest on the same demand evidence, so they form a theme future timetable envelopes can keep feeding. The ridership figures are position-grain evidence, not the leaf itself.
placements.title: The late sailing is kept where passengers still fill it and pulled earlier where they don't
placements.frame: When the timetable moves a late sailing, what ridership evidence is offered for cutting it or keeping it, and which days does it separate?
